geometry_edits.rationale: Make the hall roof read as a clearer long-span section rather than a generic faceted cap.
Keep the primary span legible along the long bar axis.
Narrow the separation so the split becomes a seam, not a fragmenting void.
Ensure the wings remain visually and structurally connected.
Reduce corner loss to retain a cleaner dominant mass while keeping a small entry articulation.

graph_edits.rationale: Shift the roof section from a generic barrel toward a clearer long-span gym profile with more explicit daylight/span expression.
Preserve the readable linear hall axis as the dominant organizational rule.
Reduce the split severity so the mass reads as one hall with a subordinate seam rather than two competing fragments.
Strengthen the connective element to make the central condition read as an intentional entry/service seam.
Soften the corner cut so it supports a cleaner anchor rather than over-fragmenting the main mass.

rationale: The candidate reads as a long bar-like gym seed with a central incision, so it has some program adjacency and a recognizable dominant axis. However, the four views reveal a split-wing mass whose center void is small and ambiguous rather than a convincing public entry/court or a robust long-span hall articulation. The roof/section logic is stepped and faceted but not yet clearly carrying span, daylight, or gymnasium interior necessity; in particular, the silhouette feels closer to an abstract split object than to one usable hall volume with subordinate support. The form is coherent across views and not obviously self-colliding, but it under-delivers on the gymnasium contract because the hall is not sufficiently unified and the ground response to the central access edge is weak.
